chunks.text: Agents shall inspect a valid identity document, capture a biometric fingerprint, and complete one-time-password verification for transactions above KES 70,000.
The Money Laundering Reporting Officer shall file suspicious agent transaction reports with the Financial Reporting Centre within twenty-four hours.
Customer identification and agent transaction records shall be retained for seven years from the most recent transaction.
Every active agent shall complete KYC and anti-money-laundering refresher training at least once every twelve months.
The Channels function shall enforce daily and single-transaction limits assigned to each agent tier.
Procurement shall complete financial, ownership, sanctions, and information-security due diligence before engaging a critical service provider.
Contracts with critical providers shall grant audit rights to the bank and the Central Bank of Kenya.
Material cyber incidents affecting a critical service shall be reported to the regulator within four hours of detection.
Treasury shall maintain a Liquidity Coverage Ratio of at least 110 percent at all times.
Treasury Risk shall perform liquidity stress testing every quarter and report results to the Board Risk Committee.
Customer complaints unresolved after five business days shall be included in the monthly complaints return.
Marketing campaigns require approval from Brand, Legal, and the relevant product owner before publication.
Enhanced customer verification for agent transactions above KES 70,000 requires identity documents, biometrics, and a one-time password.
